# Project Governance 3.0.0-rc.10.7

Long-running development no longer loses optional JEV selection at the old accounting-store
ceiling. Larger sources can contribute metadata and selected passages, and normal output clearly
distinguishes a usable local packet from successful semantic selection.

- Give decision accounting, provider admission and telemetry projection databases 512 MiB of
  physical headroom. Preserve spending counters, duplicate identities, closed scopes and retained
  history. Report `budget-store-capacity` separately from an ordinary call or byte allowance.
- Capture sources up to 16 MiB per file within a 32 MiB aggregate allowance. Apply the same local
  declaration to indexing and selected originals. Retry older oversized index omissions once;
  reuse unchanged valid facts. Keep provider request limits, sharing policy, output budgets and
  the single 45-second operation clock.
- Detect a native session bound in a different verified worktree before paid prompt selection.
  Show both locations and preserve local required guidance. Do not redirect the prompt, import
  sibling packets, change task bindings or move spending. Align the chat with its intended existing
  checkout at a pause seam; updating the package cannot reattach an existing host conversation.
- Show semantic-selection status beside packet readiness in normal commands and native prompts.
  Distinguish complete/partial answers, shadow advice and local fallback, with the owning reason.
  Valid required guidance remains usable when optional JEV selection is unavailable.

This patch does not reset databases, enable delegation, broaden project disclosure or upgrade
active worktrees automatically. Larger capacity is headroom, not indefinite retention. Source and
installed-package qualification do not establish accepted-task token or time savings.
